question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'** i.e. **'His'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 3 is **"his".**
 
• **In this context, **the pronoun is referring back to Dali's father.
 
• In English, we use **"his"** as a possessive pronoun when the noun being referred to is masculine singular.
 
• The **sentence indicates** that Dali's father was strict in the education of his children, unlike his mother, implying that his mother was not as strict.

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is: '*'Salvador Dali was a prominent Spanish surrealist painter born in Figueres, Catalonia, on 11 May 1904. Dali's father was strict in the education of his children unlike **his** mother. Dali had a brother named Salvador (4) _______ was born nine months before him and died of gastroenteritis. When he was five. Dali was taken to his brother's grave and was told that he was his brother's (5) _______.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options don't fit:
 
 
• **"Their" i**s a plural possessive pronoun, used when referring to more than one person. Since we're talking about Dali's father, a singular entity, "their" is incorrect here.
 
• **"Him"** is an object pronoun, used when the noun or pronoun it refers to is the object of the sentence. In this case, we need a possessive pronoun, not an object pronoun.
 
• **"Her" **is a possessive pronoun used when the noun being referred to is feminine singular. But the pronoun is referring back to Dali's father, a masculine noun, so "her" would not be appropriate here.
